hints: Look at two things on each curve: how high it plateaus (total volume breathed out) and how steep it is at the start (how fast air flows out).
Remember that normal lungs empty fast and fully, narrowed inflamed airways empty slowly but still reach a good total, and emphysema lungs trap air so total volume is very low.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph is showing**

This is a forced expiration after a deep breath in. The y-axis is cumulative volume breathed out in $dm^3$ and the x-axis is time in $s$. A steep curve means fast airflow. A high plateau means a large vital capacity.

Compare the three: X rises fastest and highest to about $4.7 \ dm^3$, Y rises slowly but eventually reaches about $4.3 \ dm^3$, Z plateaus very low at about $1.3 \ dm^3$.

**Spot the normal lung**

A healthy person with elastic lungs and open airways can blow out quickly and with force, so volume shoots up and plateaus high. That matches X perfectly. So X is normal lung function.

**Separate the two lung diseases**

Chronic bronchitis means inflamed bronchi and bronchioles with excess mucus. Airways are narrowed, so air flows out slowly, giving a shallow slope, but alveoli are still mostly intact so total volume is only slightly reduced. That matches Y.

Emphysema means alveolar walls are broken down, surface area is lost and elastic recoil is lost. Lungs cannot empty properly and much air stays trapped inside, so total volume breathed out is greatly reduced. That matches Z.

**Match to the table**

Chronic bronchitis = Y, emphysema = Z, normal = X. That is option C.

options.A: X cannot be chronic bronchitis because X is the fastest and largest expiration, which is normal, not obstructed.
options.B: X cannot be emphysema and Z cannot be normal because X has the highest volume and Z has the lowest volume, the opposite way round.
options.C: Correct. X is normal (fast, high volume), Y is chronic bronchitis (slow flow due to mucus and narrowing but good total), Z is emphysema (very low total due to loss of elasticity and trapped air).
options.D: Z cannot be chronic bronchitis and Y cannot be emphysema because Y reaches a near normal total while Z is severely reduced, so Z fits emphysema better.
